result.title: Investment Consultant 2025 RFP Draft.pdf
result.summary: TRS seeks bids for general investment consulting, private-markets consulting, or both, with five-year contracts and annual renewals. The RFP specifies service scopes, qualifications, questionnaires, deliverables, bundled or separate fixed-fee pricing, private-fund fees, expenses, optional value-added offers, and third-party vendor disclosures. It sets submission deadlines, formats, required forms and certifications, amendment and question procedures, confidentiality rules, limited exceptions, bid revisions, evaluation and award procedures, and restrictions including no finder’s fees or prohibited communications. The draft also provides Oklahoma’s contract terms on scope and renewal, document priority and changes, ordering, acceptance, warranties, invoicing and payment, insurance, taxes, legal compliance, audits, data confidentiality and security, conflicts, subcontracting, background checks, intellectual property, indemnification, liability limits, funding and other termination rights, suspension, force majeure, notices, transition, publicity, open records, survival, and entire agreement. Bidder forms cover business and contact details, registration, workers’ compensation, boycott disclosures, veteran status, and signatures; additional provisions address gratuities, import/export controls, and approval and replacement of key personnel.

nodes.title: Investment Consultant 2025 RFP Draft.pdf (intro)
nodes.summary: The Teachers’ Retirement System of Oklahoma (TRS) seeks proposals under RFP 715-25-1002, dated November 19, 2025, for general investment consulting, private-markets consulting, or both at a bundled fee. General services cover strategic advice, manager oversight, portfolio and manager reporting, investment-policy monitoring and advice, and attending in-person committee and Board meetings. Private-markets services cover research and manager searches. Contracts are five years with annual renewals. Proposals are due January 14, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. CST/CDT by emailed PDF to Kristen Banta, with the specified subject line and bidder identification details. The document lists required proposal materials, including forms, disclosures, specifications responses, questionnaires and Excel tables, references, fees, value-added offers, and third-party vendor information. Bidders must complete the applicable questionnaire sections and tables; general fees are fixed annually, while private-markets fees are fixed annually plus per-fund fees above four. A bundled discount may be offered. The Board may reject proposals, change the RFP before the deadline, and does not reimburse preparation costs; submissions become TRS property and are publicly inspectable. The RFP must not be altered. Signature, date, name, and title are required.

nodes.title: Investment Consultant Bid Options and Requirements
key_items: We will bid for Private Market Investment Consultant ☐
nodes.summary: The page asks bidders to indicate whether they will bid for the General Investment Consultant, Private Markets Investment Consultant, or both. General-only bidders complete questionnaire questions G.1–G.8 and the General Investment Consultant Questionnaire Table.xlsx, with annual fixed-fee pricing. Private Markets-only bidders complete G.1–G.4 and G.9–G.10 and the Private Markets Investment Consultant Questionnaire Table.xlsx, with an annual fixed fee plus a per-fund fee for more than four funds. Bidders for both mandates complete G.1–G.10 and both questionnaire tables, with the respective pricing terms; they may offer TRS a bundled-fee discount if selected for both.

nodes.title: We will bid for Both General and Private Market Investment Consultant ☐
nodes.summary: The form indicates a bid for both General and Private Market Investment Consultant services, with fields for an authorized signature, submission date, printed name, and title. General provisions define acquisition, amendment, bid, bidder, contract, debarment, indemnified parties, solicitation, State, supplier/vendor, suspension, supplier confidential information, and value-added offerings. Solicitation amendments must be posted at the same online link, and bidders must check TRS’s website regularly, at least the day before closing; TRS is not responsible for missed amendments. Bids must follow the instructions, include required bidder information, certification, and other forms, and be emailed electronically to Kristen Banta; receipt confirmation may be requested. Submit searchable PDF files and required Excel spreadsheets. Bids must use the labeled sections and format specified in A.4, avoid duplicate content, and mark any inapplicable section “Not Applicable,” “N/A,” or similar; other formats may be rejected.

nodes.title: General Provisions: Definitions and Solicitation Amendments
key_items: A.2. 1. Any Amendment shall be set forth at the same online link as the Solicitation.
nodes.summary: Defines acquisition (items or services obtained by purchase, lease, lease-purchase, or rental); amendment (written contract-document change executed by Vendor and State); bid and bidder; contract; debarment and suspension; indemnified parties; solicitation and its bid, proposal, or quotation forms; State; supplier/vendor; supplier confidential information; and value-added goods or services offered beyond Section D requirements. Debarment may bar supplier-list inclusion, bidding, quotes, and awards, and may cancel existing contracts; suspension limits supplier-list inclusion, bidding, and state contract eligibility. Confidential supplier information must be clearly marked and approved, subject to contractual and Open Records Act exclusions. Solicitation amendments must appear at the same online link. Bidders must regularly check TRS’s website, at least the day before closing; TRS is not responsible if a bidder fails to review required amendments.

nodes.title: A.3. Bid Submission
nodes.summary: Bids must comply with bidder instructions and include the completed Responding Bidder Information, Bidder’s Certification, and any other required forms. Submit electronically to Kristen Banta at Kristen.Banta@trs.ok.gov; bidders may request receipt confirmation. Bids should be provided as a searchable PDF and an Excel spreadsheet for the required attachment. Structure the bid in clearly labeled sections following the A.4 Bid Packet Format; other formats may not be accepted. Avoid duplicating content across sections, and mark any inapplicable section “Not Applicable,” “N/A,” or similarly.

nodes.title: A.4 Bid Packet Format
nodes.summary: The bid packet must include: (1) a dated cover page or transmittal letter identifying the solicitation and bidder, providing contact details, and stating whether the bid covers general services, private markets services, or both; (2) an executive summary with marketing, official-notice contact, company, and other relevant information; (3) required forms, certifications, supporting documents, insurance certificates, and disclosures of public-contract performance issues, relevant relationships or contacts, State employee connections or ownership, and actual or potential conflicts of interest, which may lead to rejection or contract termination; and (4) a list of bid portions requested to be confidential. Confidentiality requests must identify specific information, cite legal grounds under OAC 260:115-3-9, and explain why disclosure is not in the public interest. Bids become State property; confidentiality after award is limited by law, and a bid cannot be marked wholly confidential. Confidential material not listed in this section will not be considered confidential; the source text ends mid-sentence.

nodes.title: 5 | P a g e
nodes.summary: Confidentiality claims may be disclosed under state law if they fail OAC 260:115-3-9; the State need not review the entire bid for such claims. Section Five requires requested RFP exceptions or revisions to Attachment A terms to be submitted as Word documents with Track Changes, or a page stating none apply. Clarification questions are not exceptions and will be disregarded. Exceptions should not exceed 10% of State terms; excessive requests may disqualify the bid. Exceptions elsewhere, in another format, or stated generally without proposed wording or identifying terms for omission will not be considered. Section Six requires additional bidder terms to be submitted in Word in that section and harmonized with the solicitation; conflicting terms must be requested as Section Five exceptions, and unresolved conflicts may cause disqualification. The State need not search the bid for additional terms, will disregard terms submitted elsewhere, and rejects terms in unattached documents or hyperlinks. Contract documents such as ordering templates must be included in the bid; the State and customers need not execute documents that were not included.

Requested exceptions or revisions to RFP Attachment A terms must be submitted in Word with track changes; if none are requested, include a page marking the section not applicable. Clarification questions are not exceptions and will be disregarded. Exceptions should not exceed 10% of the State’s terms, and exceeding that limit may lead to disqualification. The State need not search the entire bid for exceptions; those placed elsewhere or not in the required format will not be considered. General disagreement without proposed alternative wording or a request to intentionally omit the term will also be disregarded.

nodes.title: Section Six: Additional Bidder Terms
nodes.summary: Section Six requires requested additional terms in Word format, harmonized with the Solicitation or submitted as exceptions in Section Five; unharmonized terms without documented exceptions may disqualify a Bid. Only terms submitted there are considered; the State rejects terms in unattached documents or hyperlinks and will not execute extra documents, so needed templates must be included. Section Seven addresses responses to Sections D and E requirements, including deliverable timelines. Section Eight pricing is nonconfidential, follows Section I and Attachment A, and must include travel costs. Early-payment discounts may be offered for payment periods from 10 to 30 days in five-day increments, at half- or whole-percent rates of at least 0.5%; the State need not use them. Section Nine allows priced value-added offers, without purchase obligation. Section Ten requires third-party history, relationship, joint clients, and proposed services and integration. Questions go by email to Kristen Banta by the stated deadline; consolidated answers appear on the TRS website only. Investment-consultant selection is exempt from statutory bidding but follows Board policy. Finder’s fees are prohibited and must be disclaimed. Bid changes require a superseding submission by the original method before the deadline. Respondents and subcontractors certify they are not debarred, suspended, ineligible, or excluded.

nodes.summary: Section Seven requires bidders to show how they meet or exceed applicable RFP specifications and requirements and to provide deliverable timelines when applicable. Section Eight covers pricing, which is not confidential; pricing must follow Section I and Attachment A and include all contract travel expenses, such as transportation, lodging, and meals. Early-payment discounts may be considered and must state percentages for payment periods of at least 10 days, in five-day increments through 30 days; percentages must be in half- or whole-percent amounts, with a 0.5% minimum. The State need not use a discount. Section Nine covers optional value-added products or services, which must include pricing and relevant information; the State is not obligated to purchase them. Section Ten is titled Third Party Vendor Information.

nodes.summary: For each third-party vendor or subcontractor, bids must describe its history, relationship to the bidder, shared clients, and role in the proposed solution. The section sets Q&A and bid-revision procedures, prohibits finder’s fees, requires responsibility certifications and disclosure of any inability to certify, and covers bid opening, confidentiality, late bids, firm fiscal-year pricing, negotiation, rejection, awards, vendor registration, and contract terms. It describes TRS, its governance, investments, and manager-search process; restricts communications with TRS; and outlines consulting services, minimum qualifications, and extensive firm, staff, regulatory, technical, and service questionnaire disclosures. It provides submission and selection timelines, evaluation criteria, separate or bundled pricing, fee and expense rules, and general-consultant duties. Private-market assumptions specify search volumes, diligence, reporting, meetings, exclusions, and coordination. Attachment A introduces the State’s general contract terms.

nodes.title: Bid Requirements, Questions, and Changes
nodes.summary: For each third-party vendor or subcontractor included in a bid, provide its company history, relationship to the bidder, clients the parties have served together, and proposed products or services and how they integrate with the bidder’s solution. Solicitation questions must be emailed to Kristen Banta by the stated deadline; TRS will consolidate questions and answers into one document and post it on its website by the deadline, with no other distribution method. Investment consultant selection is exempt from Oklahoma statutory competitive bidding procedures but remains subject to the Board’s procurement policy requiring competitive bids. Vendors must certify that no finder’s fee or commission has been or will be paid. To revise a bid before the response deadline, submit a replacement to Kristen Banta by the original submission method, stating that it supersedes the previously submitted bid.

nodes.title: A.7. Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, and Other Responsibility Matters
nodes.summary: Respondents certify that they and their principals/subcontractors are not debarred or excluded; have no specified fraud, criminal, antitrust, or related convictions or civil judgments in the prior three years; are not currently charged with such offenses; and have not had public contracts terminated for cause/default in the prior three years. Any inability to certify requires an explanation. Bids will be opened by the Business Manager with a witness at the stated TRS offices as soon as practical after the deadline. Under Oklahoma open-records law, bids remain confidential until contract award or solicitation cancellation. Late bids are rejected. A submitted bid is a legal offer and, upon acceptance, forms a contract under Attachment A. Prices must remain firm at least 180 days and be stated by fiscal year. The Board may negotiate with any, all, or no respondents to secure best value; offers and supporting data may be revised or requested, but RFP requirements remain fixed unless TRS/Board finds changes serve the State’s interest. TRS/Board may reject noncompliant bids or bids imposing terms or conditions.

nodes.title: Bid Procedures, Contract Terms, and Certifications
nodes.summary: The certification states that participants have not recently been convicted or found liable for specified fraud, contracting, or other offenses; are not currently charged with those offenses; and have not had public contracts terminated for cause or default within three years. Participants unable to certify must explain why. Bids are opened by the Business Manager with a witness at the specified TRS office as soon as reasonably practical after the deadline. Under Oklahoma open-records law, bids remain confidential until contract award or solicitation cancellation. Late bids are rejected. An accepted bid becomes a contract, subject to Attachment A. Pricing must be firm for at least 180 days and quoted by fiscal year, with further terms in Section I and Attachment A. The Board may negotiate with any number of respondents to secure best value; negotiations may revise offer terms and require supporting data, but RFP requirements remain unchanged unless TRS or the Board finds a change in the State’s best interest. Inflexibility may disadvantage a firm.

nodes.title: A.15. Award of Contract
nodes.summary:
A.15. Award of Contract
The Board may award the Contract to more than one bidder by awarding the Contract(s) by item or groups of items, or may award the Contract on an ALL OR NONE basis, whichever is deemed by the Board to be in the best interest of the State of Oklahoma. In order to receive an award or payments from TRS, vendors must be registered. The vendor registration process can be completed electronically through the OMES website at the following link: https://oklahoma.gov/omes/divisions/central-purchasing/suppliers- and-payees/supplier-portal.html .The initial contract term will begin July 1, 2026, and continue through June 30, 2027 (Fiscal Year 2027). The contract may be renewed for up to four (4) additional one-year periods at the Board's discretion

nodes.title: B. TRS BACKGROUND INFORMATION
key_items: B.1. Legal Authorization; B.2. Board Composition; B.3. Asset Allocation
B.5. Investment Guidelines; B.6. Investment Manager Search Process; B.7. Private Market Reporting Process
nodes.summary: Oklahoma’s Teachers’ Retirement System (TRS), established in 1943 under state law, provides retirement benefits to public educators. Its Board and 52 budgeted staff administer the system and oversee approximately $26 billion in investments, aiming to grow and protect funds needed for member obligations; the Executive Director is the chief administrative officer. The Board has 14 voting members representing state education and finance officials and gubernatorial and legislative appointees, plus one nonvoting retired-educator representative. Target allocation as of July 1, 2025: U.S. equity 32.4%, international equity 14.1%, fixed income 25%, real assets 11% (real estate 8%, infrastructure 3%), private equity 10%, and private debt 7.5%. External managers manage all assets. TRS provides links to its manager list and Investment Policy Statement. Manager searches use competitive invitations to bid, a streamlined process without a standard questionnaire, staff/consultant blackout, or formulaic scoring, but with a Board blackout. Meketa Investment Group handles private-market reporting, fee validation, and capital calls; these services are not required for this search.

nodes.title: C. COMMUNICATION WITH TRS
nodes.summary: TRS will answer only questions submitted under Section A.5; telephone questions are not accepted. During the RFP, prospective providers may not contact TRS Board members, consultants, or staff directly, except for normal incumbent-provider business unrelated to the selection. From RFP release until vendor selection and contract execution and approval, RFP communications must follow the A.5 Q&A process, with exceptions for identified TRS staff and designated participants during negotiations, presentations, and contract award and execution. Bidders must disclose any prohibited communications in writing to TRS’s General Counsel before the contract-award board meeting. Violations may result in proposal rejection.

nodes.title: D. SOLICITATION SPECIFICATIONS, MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS, AND TIMELINE
key_items: D.1. General Investment Consultant Services Requested; D.1. 1. Strategic Advisory
D.1. General Investment Consultant Services Requested
D.1. 2. Investment Search and Manager Oversight
D.1. 3. Reporting & Board Meetings; D.1. 5. Other Services; D.2. Private Market Consultant Services Requested

D.3. Minimum Qualifications – General Investment Consultant
D.4. Minimum Qualifications – Private Market Consultant
nodes.summary: The RFP seeks general and private-market investment consulting services for Oklahoma TRS. General services include periodic asset-liability studies and allocation advice; capital-market, liquidity, pacing, peer-comparison, and rebalancing analysis; public-market manager searches, monitoring, retention advice, due diligence, fee reviews, research databases, and guideline support. Consultants must prepare monthly and quarterly performance reports for Board and Investment Committee meetings (about eight each annually), analyze performance, attribution, risk, and proxy-voting policy compliance, and provide special reports. They also support Investment Policy Statement monitoring and updates, records requests, trustee education, retreats, custodian and securities-lending reviews, and other assignments. Private-market services cover searches and sourcing across private equity, credit, real estate, and infrastructure; market research, account structuring, due diligence, meeting support, an annual portfolio review, and advice on post-closing matters. General consultants must be SEC-registered, serve five U.S. public pensions each with at least $10 billion, act as fiduciaries, follow TRS policy, and annually disclose conflicts, revenue, and affiliations. Private consultants must be SEC-registered, advise on at least $20 billion in private assets, cover specified asset classes, review the discretionary private-equity manager, and meet fiduciary and disclosure requirements.

nodes.title: E. QUESTIONNAIRE
nodes.summary: The questionnaire seeks firm and team profiles, including services, finances, ownership, organization, leadership continuity, ethics, outsourcing, staff qualifications and assignments, client responsibilities, compensation, and asset-class experience. Regulatory and due-diligence disclosures cover investigations, misconduct, conflicts, gifts, SEC registration, discretionary and OCIO services, fees, insurance, data sales, cybersecurity, disaster readiness, references, and terminated clients. General Consultant bidders must address asset-liability modeling, strategic allocation, capital-market assumptions, liquidity forecasting, risk measurement, asset-class design, manager research and monitoring, transitions, fees, private-market accounts, technology, reporting, peer data, IPS compliance, Northern Trust experience, and AI. Required materials include reports, platform screenshots, client lists, due-diligence examples, historical assumptions, questionnaire spreadsheets, and confirmation of reviewing specified TRS materials. Private Market Search bidders must describe deployment, investment style, research, technology, due diligence, portfolio and benchmark practices, GP familiarity, client structures, and discounts, and provide relevant reports, metrics, and submissions. The section also specifies proposal deadlines and selection, presentation, and contract-start dates.

nodes.title: Consultant Firm and Team Questionnaire
nodes.summary: This questionnaire section, for General Investment Consultant and Private Market Search Consultant bidders, requests a firm overview and team overview. Firm questions cover identifying and contact information, history, services and revenue by business line, ownership and financial condition, organizational charts and office functions, past and expected restructuring or leadership changes, succession and leadership continuity, ethics and CFA Institute standards, outsourced functions, and the firm’s key competitive advantage. Team questions cover the TRS relationship team’s roles, biographies, locations, education, certifications and work histories; each member’s current accounts, client responsibilities, account counts, locations and assets under management; compensation and incentives; and experience advising across the System’s invested asset classes.

nodes.title: E.3. Regulatory and Ethics
nodes.summary: The section requests regulatory and ethics disclosures covering investigations or proceedings; personnel misconduct or convictions; conflicts involving Oklahoma Teachers’ Retirement System stakeholders; gifts or expenses to its officials; SEC registration and Form ADV materials; conflicts and manager disclosures for discretionary management; OCIO AUM, clients and staffing; fee-based services to investment managers; insurance coverage; sale of client data; discretionary services and client base; disaster recovery, remote-work readiness and cybersecurity breaches. It also requires three comparable fund references and details of any consulting client that terminated the firm within three years, including contact information, reason and assets advised. General Consultant bidders must describe asset-liability modeling capabilities, actuary credentials and a sample study; strategic asset-allocation recommendations; capital-market expectations and third-party research; liquidity and cash-flow forecasting; fund-level risk measurement; and asset-class structuring, including relationships, portfolio design, mandate sizes and risk-return profiles.

nodes.title: Consultant Due Diligence and Strategic Advisory Capabilities
key_items: E.5. 5. Explain how fund-level risk is measured and monitored.
nodes.summary: The page requests firm disclosures on legal or regulatory misconduct, conflicts of interest, gifts to Oklahoma TRS personnel, SEC registration and Form ADV materials, discretionary-management conflicts and disclosures, OCIO scale and staffing, paid services to investment managers, insurance coverage, client-data sales, discretionary services and client base, disaster recovery and remote-work readiness, and cybersecurity practices and breaches. It asks for three comparable fund references and details of any client that terminated the firm in the past three years. For general consultant bidders, it covers asset-liability modeling expertise and a sample study; strategic asset-allocation recommendations; capital-market expectations and third-party research; liquidity and cash-flow forecasting; fund-level risk measurement and monitoring; and asset-class structuring, including relationships, portfolio design, mandate sizes, and risk-return profiles.

nodes.title: 13 | P a g e
nodes.summary: The text requests high-level review of strategic asset allocation and portfolio improvements, followed by details on public-market manager research, team organization, selection tracking, analytics, active versus passive approaches, termination criteria, asset transitions, expense control and fee negotiation, aggregation discounts and agreements, client research, and customized private-market separately managed accounts. It asks about technology available to TRS; performance reporting metrics, controls, systems, customization, and turnaround; peer-fund data sources and availability; IPS-compliance monitoring; Northern Trust reporting experience; and AI tools and client implementations. Required submissions include sample public- and private-market performance reports, online-platform screenshots and overview, a representative client list, an unredacted public-equity manager due-diligence report if possible, current and 2020/2015 capital-market assumptions, a completed questionnaire spreadsheet, and confirmation of review of TRS’s specified investment and performance reports.

nodes.title: Investment Consulting Research, Reporting, and Submissions
key_items: E.6. Public Market Investment Manager Research and Monitoring
E.7. 1. What systems and tools do you provide that will be available to TRS?
nodes.summary: Requests high-level review of TRS’s strategic asset allocation and portfolio improvement opportunities. Covers public-market manager research, selection and monitoring processes, research organization and track records; available analytics; active versus passive approaches; manager termination and asset transitions; expense control, fee negotiation and discounts; research provided; and private-market separately managed accounts. Asks about systems and tools, performance reporting metrics, controls, customization and timing, peer data, Investment Policy Statement compliance monitoring, Northern Trust experience, and AI use. Required submissions include sample public- and private-market performance reports, online-platform screenshots and overview, a representative client list, an unredacted public-equity due diligence report if possible, capital market assumptions from the present, 2020 and 2015, a completed questionnaire spreadsheet, and confirmation of review of specified TRS investment and performance reports.

nodes.title: 14 | P a g e
nodes.summary: Private Market Search Consultant bidders must describe their experience and historical private-market deployment; investment style and advantages; research capacity and quality; technology; investment and operational due diligence (including prior-year fund counts and asset classes); portfolio management, benchmark use, and diversification; familiarity with TRS general partners; client relationship structures (discretionary/non-discretionary, fund-of-one, commingled, and possible alternatives); and aggregation discounts and relationships. Required materials include online-platform screenshots and overview, an allowable representative client list, an unredacted example due-diligence report on a closed-end real estate fund no longer fundraising, the completed questionnaire spreadsheet, relevant historical performance metrics, and confirmation of review of five specified TRS investment and performance reports. Proposals are due January 14, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. CT; late or misdirected submissions are rejected, and extensions are unavailable. Timeline: solicitation issued November 19, 2025; questions due December 10; Q&A posted December 19; finalists selected February 20, 2026; presentations, if needed, April 21–22; tentative contract start July 1, 2026.

nodes.title: Private Market Consultant Submission Requirements
key_items: E.9. 2. Describe your overall investment style. What are your competitive advantages?
E.9. 7. Describe your level of familiarity with the general partners TRS is currently invested with.
nodes.summary: Private Market Search Consultant bidders must describe their manager-search experience across TRS asset classes and private-market capital deployment; investment style and advantages; research capabilities; technology; investment and operational due diligence, including recent fund counts and asset classes; portfolio management, benchmarks, and diversification; familiarity with TRS’s current general partners; client engagement models and potentially beneficial structures; and consultant aggregation discounts and relationships. Additional submissions include online-platform screenshots and overview; an allowable representative client list; an unredacted example due diligence report for a closed-end real estate fund no longer fundraising (other reports welcome); the completed consultant questionnaire spreadsheet; relevant historical performance metrics for buy-list and discretionary funds and other available measures; and confirmation of review of TRS’s specified investment, financial, and performance reports.

nodes.title: F. Solicitation Deadline and Timeline
key_items: I. 1.12. All other anticipated projects as covered in the Scope of Assignment in Section D1..
nodes.summary: Completed proposals are due by 4:00 p.m. CT January 14, 2026; late or misdirected proposals are rejected, and extensions will not be granted. Timeline: RFP issued Nov. 19, 2025; questions due Dec. 10; answers posted Dec. 19; finalist selection Feb. 20, 2026; finalist presentations, if needed, Apr. 21–22; tentative contract start July 1, 2026. Both consultant procurements are evaluated for best value based on service capability, firm and team expertise and track record, regulatory and ethical record, contract exceptions or additional terms, fees, interviews/presentation, and references. General-consultant criteria also cover strategic advice, manager research/monitoring, and technology/reporting; private-market criteria include manager searches and technology/research. Fees cover a five-year period, beginning July 1, 2026, with annual fixed fees; expenses are not reimbursed. Bids may cover either service or both, with separate and bundled pricing. Private-market and bundled bids add a per-fund fee above four funds. General-consultant duties include eight Board and eight committee meetings yearly, portfolio performance reporting, an asset-liability study every four years or after an experience study, and as-needed public manager searches without extra fees; other Section D1 projects are included.

nodes.title: I. 2. Private Market Consultant Assumptions
nodes.summary: The RFP fee proposal will help determine the selected vendor. It must cover the full range of private-market consulting services, with annual fees for July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 and each of the next four contract years; annual fixed fees may vary, but the per-search fee above four must remain fixed. Assume four searches yearly—three closed-end and one evergreen—with additional searches charged per fund/search. TRS will generally use the consultant’s sourcing pipeline; outside-pipeline due diligence is expected only once or twice over the contract. Provide access to buy-rated private credit, real estate, and infrastructure diligence reports; operational diligence is required only for funds selected for commitment. Private-equity research is unnecessary, but review the discretionary private-equity partner annually for performance, fees, and portfolio structure. Attend one in-person annual portfolio review and fund recommendation meetings in person or virtually. Investments are non-discretionary; exclude comprehensive legal review, cash-flow management, consolidated reporting, and pacing models. Work collaboratively with TRS’s back-office provider and general consultant.

nodes.title: 17 | P a g e
nodes.summary:
17 | P a g eAttachment A
This State of Oklahoma General Terms ("General Terms") is a contract document in connection with the contract awarded by the Teachers’ Retirement System of Oklahoma (TRS).
In addition to other terms contained in an applicable contract document, supplier and TRS agree to the following General Terms:

nodes.title: 1. Scope and Contract Renewal
nodes.summary: The supplier may not add products or services without the state’s prior written approval, which may require competitive bidding, and must contact the state about needs outside the contract’s scope. The supplier cannot obligate customers to pay without a signed encumbering document or beyond the award amount, and is not entitled to payment for unrequested or unsatisfactorily accepted offerings. Before renewal, TRS may review the contract’s value, supplier performance, legal terms, pricing, discounts, and current offerings; required changes must be documented in a good-faith amendment. The state may extend the contract for 90 days at the contract rate with written notice before expiration, and may choose further 90-day extensions, where lawful, to finalize a new award or transition suppliers. The supplier must maintain its annually expiring state registration as a condition of renewal.

nodes.title: 2. Contract Effectiveness and Order of Priority
nodes.summary: The contract takes effect when last signed unless otherwise agreed in writing; the supplier may not act or incur obligations beforehand. Documents are complementary, with amendments highest priority, followed by the contract, contract-specific state terms, solicitation, compliant negotiated bid, and mutually agreed work documents. Supplier-provided terms cannot override state/customer protections unless amended. Documents may be typed or written and transactions may be electronic. Changes require an amendment; unilateral or oral changes are void, as are unexecuted supplier ordering terms. Contract information is generally disclosable except legally protected confidential information; linked, reseller, or other terms cannot alter protections or conflict with law. State agencies are tax-exempt, supplier taxes are unreimbursed, travel is included in price, and product pricing includes prepaid shipping and handling, with possible customer charges for expedited delivery. Orders require valid purchasing mechanisms and remain governed by the contract. Services require customer acceptance, with no automatic deemed acceptance. Products and deliverables carry a warranty against defects and faulty workmanship for at least 90 days after acceptance or the manufacturer’s longer maximum period; defects are to be repaired.

nodes.title: Contract Changes and Pricing Requirements
key_items: 3. Modification of contract Terms and contract documents
nodes.summary: Related document transactions may be conducted electronically under Oklahoma’s Uniform Electronic Transactions Act. Contract changes require a mutually executed amendment; unilateral supplier changes and oral statements have no effect, and unauthorized changes create no claim. Supplier ordering-document terms are void unless mutually executed, and TRS is not liable for supplier performance or payment obligations to others. Contract information is generally public unless legally protected as confidential. Conflicting external or third-party terms cannot override the contract, increase state or customer liability, or reduce their rights without TRS’s written agreement; terms conflicting with applicable law are unenforceable, and signing does not waive the law. State agencies are exempt from specified state taxes, and state agencies and political subdivisions from federal excise taxes; supplier taxes are not reimbursed. Supplier travel costs must be included in the acquisition price. Prices include prepaid shipping, packaging, delivery, and handling, with delivery to the customer’s destination and no standard shipping surcharge; customers may pay for requested expedited or special delivery.

nodes.title: 5. Ordering, Inspection and Acceptance
nodes.summary: Products and services must be ordered using a valid purchase order, payment mechanism, or purchase card, and all transactions follow the contract; orders issued before expiration or termination remain binding unless otherwise agreed in writing. Services must meet industry best practices and require customer acceptance; acceptance is not automatic upon delivery or performance. Products and deliverables are warranted to be substantially uninterrupted and error-free, and free from material and workmanship defects for at least 90 days after acceptance or the manufacturer’s maximum warranty period, whichever is longer; defects must be repaired or replaced at no cost. Products are subject to inspection and acceptance at destination, with title, risk, and pre-acceptance damage claims remaining the supplier’s responsibility. Payment is not final acceptance; confirmed nonconformities or latent defects require supplier-funded replacement or a refund, without limiting other remedies. Deliveries must meet required dates, with possible liquidated damages for delay. Changes require written customer authorization, and replacement service staff must be comparably or better qualified; transition staff must be capable. Warranty and return terms cannot be less favorable or more costly than those offered to similar customers.

nodes.title: 6. Invoices and Payment
nodes.summary: Payment is due at contract prices after products or services are provided and accepted, upon receipt of a proper invoice compliant with Oklahoma law. Invoices must include the purchase order number, description, and provision dates; improper or late invoices may delay processing. Fees are payable net 45 days unless an early-payment discount is negotiated. Late-payment interest is governed by state law and is the sole remedy; other late fees are prohibited. Discount periods begin upon receipt of a proper invoice, but the state need not take a discount. Subsequent payments may be adjusted to correct overpayments or underpayments, with written notice to the supplier. The supplier has no setoff right. Invoices must be submitted within six months after the fiscal year in which goods or services were provided, and the supplier must accept purchase-card payment as permitted by Oklahoma law.

nodes.title: 7. Maintenance of lnsurance, Payment of Taxes, and Workers' Compensation
nodes.summary: The supplier and approved subcontractors must obtain required insurance at their own expense from carriers rated A- or better and provide proof before starting work; proof is also required when personnel or vehicles are used at customer premises or for contract work. Policies must provide cancellation notice, name the state and its agencies as certificate holder, and evidence renewals or changes. Coverage must continue until contractual obligations end; primary and excess/umbrella policies may meet limits. Minimums are workers’ compensation and employers’ liability as required by law; commercial general liability of $2 million per occurrence; auto liability of $2 million combined single limit per accident; and, when handling state data, security/privacy liability of $5 million per occurrence. Additional written coverage may be required. The supplier is responsible for its and its personnel’s taxes and legal compliance, including wage, insurance, and workers’ compensation laws; the customer and state provide no related taxes, unemployment insurance, workers’ compensation, or employee benefits. The supplier must indemnify the customer, state, and related parties for associated liabilities, claims, and costs, including reasonable attorneys’ fees.

nodes.title: 8. Compliance With Applicable Laws
nodes.summary: The supplier must continuously comply with applicable laws and regulations, including requirements concerning drug-free workplaces, environmental protection, debarment, civil rights and accessibility, lobbying, federal tax information, independent audits, immigration verification, privacy and security, and state business registration and taxes. Supplier personnel and subcontractors must follow customer and applicable state policies; the supplier must communicate these requirements and provide evidence of compliance when requested. Required licenses and permits must be maintained at no extra cost, and funding-related mandatory contract terms and applicable state tobacco-use executive orders must be followed. The supplier represents that contract performance will not conflict with third-party agreements, it can pay debts and does not anticipate bankruptcy or receivership, and known litigation or claims have been disclosed. Electronic communications must meet accessibility standards; noncompliant materials must be corrected and redelivered, and accessible alternate formats provided on request, without additional cost.

nodes.title: 9. Audits and Records Clause
nodes.summary: The clause broadly defines “records” to include documents, media, computer data, accounting practices, and other data in any form. Relevant federal or state agencies and customer governing entities may audit and examine records related to contract execution and performance at no cost to the customer, excluding supplier costs included in contract pricing unless otherwise agreed. The supplier must retain contract records throughout the contract and for seven years after completion or termination, unless the contract specifies otherwise. If a claim, audit, litigation, or other action begins before that period ends, records must be kept until two years after all related issues are resolved or the seven-year period ends, whichever is later. For professional services, related supplier records are subject to examination by the state agency, state auditor and inspector, and state purchasing director.

nodes.title: 10. Confidentiality
nodes.summary: The supplier must protect state and citizen data under applicable laws, use it only to perform the contract, maintain a proven security system, and prevent disclosure without the customer’s prior written approval except as necessary for services or required by law. It must bind all personnel and subcontractors with access to equivalent confidentiality restrictions. The supplier must immediately report known or reasonably suspected unauthorized data use or disclosure, promptly provide details, assist with investigation and prevention, cooperate in related proceedings, and bear breach response and recovery costs, including at least three years of credit monitoring, notices, and call-center services. It must promptly prevent recurrence. Improper disclosure may cause irreparable harm, entitling the customer to immediate injunctive or other remedies without a cure period. Third-party data requests must be immediately forwarded to the state purchasing director and other designated contacts, with cooperation to protect the data. Supplier confidential information may be disclosed as permitted by Oklahoma’s Open Records Act; contract terms and information are otherwise disclosable unless state law or policy deems them confidential.

nodes.title: 11. Conflict of Interest
nodes.summary: The supplier, its employees, agents, and subcontractors must disclose outside activities or interests that conflict or may conflict with the state’s best interests, in addition to any legal or professional ethics requirements. Prompt disclosure is required for interests related directly or indirectly to anyone doing or seeking business with the state, state employees, or third parties awarded state contracts. While contractual obligations remain, planning, preparing for, or engaging in such activities requires the state’s prior written approval. The state may terminate all or part of the contract at its sole discretion for a conflict of interest. The supplier may not receive compensation based on capital gains or appreciation of funds it recommends TRS invest or commit.

nodes.title: 12. Assignment and Permitted Subcontractors
nodes.summary: Supplier may not assign or transfer contract obligations without the state’s prior written consent; payment-right assignments require timely notice to the state and affected customers. Assignments tied to specified mergers, equity sales, or asset sales are allowed if the successor assumes all obligations and prior notice is given; unlawful assignments are void. Supplier remains responsible for subcontractors, payments, and performance, and must obtain the state’s discretionary written approval of subcontractors and applicable employees, provide proposal details and a binding written subcontract, and maintain approval (which the state may revoke). Payments go to supplier, except for assigned payments, and are barred for unapproved personnel; state or customer rights may be transferred to other customer entities at no extra cost. Required background checks may delay access; costs, coordination, replacement, and possible termination are addressed. Prices include third-party intellectual-property royalties; supplier must secure continued use, provide noninfringing replacements or services, or refund relevant costs, without limiting other remedies. Oklahoma cannot indemnify private contractors; supplier’s stated duty includes defending and indemnifying parties against third-party claims and losses.

nodes.title: Subcontracting, Background Checks, and Intellectual Property
key_items: 13. Background Checks and Criminal History Investigations
nodes.summary: Suppliers must obtain written subcontractor agreements imposing applicable contract obligations and certifications, maintain them, and secure prior state approval for subcontractors and their employees; approval may be revoked for poor performance or misconduct. Payments go directly to the supplier, except for authorized assignments, and are not due for work by unapproved personnel. State or customer rights and obligations may be transferred to other customer entities at no added cost. Before services begin, the state may require background and criminal-history checks; access may be withheld pending acceptable results. Customers generally pay for checks beyond normal hiring practices, unless the supplier’s failure to provide acceptable existing results necessitates them. Unacceptable personnel may need replacement, or the related order or payment mechanism may be terminated. Prices include third-party intellectual-property royalties. If infringement is alleged, the supplier must enable continued use, modify or replace the affected product, or redo the service with a functional noninfringing equivalent, including remedies for materially affected related items. If no alternative is reasonably available, refunds may be required. These remedies do not exclude other legal or equitable remedies.

nodes.title: 15. Indemnification
nodes.summary: The State of Oklahoma cannot indemnify private contractors or pledge state credit. The supplier must defend and indemnify covered parties for third-party bodily injury, death, or property-damage claims caused by its or its personnel’s negligence or willful misconduct. For customer property loss caused by supplier fault, the parties must seek an equitable repair or replacement settlement, payable by the supplier within 60 days of invoice. The supplier also indemnifies for contract-representation breaches and intellectual-property infringement, subject to exclusions for customer content, certain modifications or combinations, unauthorized use, and unrelated third-party products. Parties must promptly notify one another of claims; customers reasonably cooperate, supplier uses qualified counsel, and settlements generally require the defended party’s written consent. The Oklahoma Attorney General coordinates defense when a state agency is sued and must approve settlements involving the State; supplier may participate or be authorized to control the defense. The State and customers disclaim liability to supplier for specified indirect and consequential losses, but liability limits do not cover specified injury, property damage, indemnity, security, confidentiality, or non-exempt misconduct-related liabilities.

nodes.title: Indemnity, Infringement, and Defense Procedures
nodes.summary: The supplier indemnifies covered parties for bodily injury, death, or property-damage claims arising from its or its personnel’s negligence or willful misconduct. If supplier-caused negligence or misconduct damages customer property, the parties will negotiate repair or replacement compensation when practical; the supplier pays the invoiced amount within 60 days. Supplier also indemnifies third-party claims tied to contractual warranty breaches or alleged intellectual-property infringement, subject to exceptions for customer content, unauthorized modifications or combinations, contract-violating use, and certain third-party products. Parties must promptly give written claim notice; affected customers reasonably cooperate, and supplier uses qualified counsel. Settlements generally require the defended party’s written consent, with a limited monetary-damages exception for non-state parties. For lawsuits naming a state agency, Oklahoma’s attorney general coordinates the defense or may authorize supplier control; state settlements require advance written concurrence. If supplier lacks sole control, it may participate equally and remains liable to indemnify.

nodes.title: 15.6 Limitation of Liability
nodes.summary: The contract excludes state/customer liability to the supplier for lost profits, sales, business costs or investments, goodwill loss, and indirect or other specified consequential damages. These limits do not cover supplier-caused property damage, injury or death; indemnity, security or confidentiality duties; or misconduct/negligence and liabilities that law prohibits limiting. They apply regardless of acceptance and despite a remedy’s failure, reflecting the parties’ risk allocation. The state may terminate all or part for insufficient appropriated or third-party funds on at least 15 days’ notice; its funding decision is binding. Supplier must minimize costs, refund unused prepaid fees, and is paid for accepted goods/services, but receives no further termination-related payments or damages; termination is not breach and does not release supplier liability. For cause, either side may terminate after notice of material breach and 30 days to cure, subject to partial-termination protections. The state may terminate immediately for specified compliance, serious breach, or award-administration issues, and with up to 10 days’ notice for lobbying violations by PR vendors. Termination preserves other remedies and claims. Repeated unacceptable performance, adverse unilateral terms changes, anticipated nonperformance, insolvency, creditor assignment, receivership or bankruptcy are material breaches; other contractual or legal grounds also apply.

nodes.title: 18. Termination for Convenience
key_items: 20. Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, and Other Responsibility Matters
21. Certification Regarding state Employees Prohibition From Fulfilling Services
20. Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, and Other Responsibility Matters
21. Certification Regarding state Employees Prohibition From Fulfilling Services
nodes.summary: The state may terminate all or part of the contract for convenience on at least 30 days’ written notice; the supplier must limit affected costs, receives payment for accepted goods/services, refunds unused prepaid fees, and remains liable for claims. The supplier may be suspended without advance notice for specified compliance failures, with similar cost, payment, refund and remedy rules; work resumes only when formally authorized or properly encumbered. Erroneous debarment/responsibility certifications may lead to default termination and must be reported; suppliers also certify that state employees involved in contract development or approval will not provide contract services. Force majeure excuses qualifying delays subject to mitigation and notice, but not specified supplier-system/personnel failures or confidentiality, indemnity, security and breach-notice duties; payment may be reduced or orders ended. Supplier must protect customer property and people and bear specified losses. Notices must be written and delivered as prescribed. Oklahoma law and venue apply; the contract creates no employment, requires transition cooperation and prior publicity approval, and acknowledges Open Records Act obligations and confidentiality exceptions.

nodes.title: Contract Notices and Miscellaneous Terms
nodes.summary: Notices to TRS must be sent to its General Counsel at the specified Oklahoma City address, with a copy to the Chief Investment Officer; contact details may be updated in writing, and confidentiality, breach, and termination notices cannot be sent solely by email. Oklahoma law governs contract disputes, subject to applicable federal rules for federally funded grants, and venue is Oklahoma County; the state rejects terms limiting its rights under Oklahoma law. The contract creates no employment relationship or employee benefits for supplier personnel. At expiration or termination, the supplier must provide needed transition services monthly at the contract or mutually agreed rate, propose a plan upon request, and cooperate with a successor; noncooperation may be recorded as poor performance. The contract is not an endorsement, and supplier publicity naming the state or a customer, or implying endorsement, requires submission and prior written state approval.

nodes.title: 25.5 Open Records Act
key_items: If sent to TRS:; With a copy, which shall not constitute notice, to:; 25.2 Employment Relationship; 25.3 Transition Services; 25.4 Publicity
With a copy, which shall not constitute notice, to:
nodes.summary: The provisions address: Oklahoma Open Records Act compliance, preserving the state purchasing director’s authority over confidential bid information, excluding specified public, previously known, independently developed, third-party, and state-pricing information from supplier confidential information, and allowing legally required disclosure after reasonable written notice to permit a protective remedy. Failure to enforce contract rights is not a waiver, and waiving one breach does not waive later breaches. Parties may not use each other’s marks without written consent; the contract is nonexclusive; only specified rights are granted; parties must cooperate on transitions; and required approvals may not be unreasonably delayed or withheld. Terms conflicting with mandatory law are unenforceable, without waiving applicable law. Invalid provisions are severable and may be narrowed to be enforceable. Headings are for convenience only. State sovereign immunity and other defenses are reserved. Applicable services and naturally surviving obligations—including certain payments, confidentiality, security, data-breach, and indemnification duties—continue after expiration or termination. The text ends with the heading “Entire Agreement,” without its terms.

nodes.title: General Contract Rights and Protections
nodes.summary: The confidentiality excerpt excludes information independently developed, lawfully received from an authorized third party without confidentiality restrictions, or pricing provided to the state; legally required disclosure is permitted with reasonable written notice allowing the supplier to seek protection. Failure to enforce rights is not a waiver, and waiving one breach does not waive later breaches. The parties may not use each other’s marks without written consent, may contract with others, retain all ungranted rights, must cooperate on transitions, and may not unreasonably delay or withhold required approvals. Terms conflicting with compulsory state or federal law are unenforceable, without waiving applicable law. Invalid provisions are severed or limited where possible, preserving the remainder. Headings are for convenience only. The state retains sovereign immunity and all legal rights and defenses. Applicable performance and obligations intended by nature to continue—including pre-expiration payment, confidentiality, security and data-breach, and indemnification obligations—survive expiration or termination.

key_items: 25.6 Failure to Enforce; 25.7 Mutual Responsibilities; 25.8 Invalid Term or Condition; 25.9 Severability; 25.10 Section Headings; 25.11 Sovereign Immunity; 25.12 Survival

25.13 Entire Agreement
31 | P a g eThe contract documents taken together as a whole constitute the entire agreement between the parties. No statement, promise, condition, understanding, inducement or representation, oral or written, expressed or implied, which is not contained in a contract document shall be binding or valid. The supplier's representations and certifications, including any completed electronically, are incorporated by reference into the contract.

nodes.title: 25.14 Gratuities
nodes.summary:
25.14 Gratuities
The contract may be immediately terminated, in whole or in part, by written notice if it is determined that the supplier, its employee, agent, or another representative violated any federal, state or local law, rule or ordinance by offering or giving a gratuity to any state employee directly involved in the contract. In addition, suspension or debarment of the supplier may result from such a violation.

nodes.title: 25.15 Import/Export Controls
nodes.summary: The contract requires both parties to comply with applicable import/export laws when handling contract-related goods, services, software, or technical information. Key personnel are vendor staff mutually designated by the parties. Vendor changes require TRS’s prior written approval, except for specified reasons including serious illness, mandated leave, death, disability, termination for cause (not to reassign), mutual agreement, or voluntary departure; an unauthorized change is a for-cause event. Vendor must notify TRS if a departing employee returns, and TRS may require reassignment. Replacements require TRS’s written approval, an interview option, and requested information; approval cannot be unreasonably withheld. Replacements must have substantially similar qualifications and cause no service delay, and replacement issues are not force majeure or TRS-caused delays. The bidder form requires a competitive-bid certification and solicitation, business, and contact details; disclosure of any boycott of Israeli goods or services; Oklahoma Secretary of State registration or an exemption statement; workers’ compensation insurance proof or an exemption statement; and service-disabled veteran status selection with required certification, ownership, and management evidence if applicable, followed by an authorized signature and date.

result.title: OMESformCP076.pdf
result.summary: The Oklahoma Central Purchasing forms require bidders to provide solicitation, business, tax and supplier identifiers, contact details, and an authorized signature. Bidders must disclose whether they boycott Israeli goods or services and indicate Oklahoma Secretary of State registration, providing a filing number or, before award, registration or a signed explanation of claimed exemption. They must provide workers’ compensation insurance proof or a signed, dated letterhead statement explaining an exemption. Service-disabled veteran businesses must provide federal status certification and evidence of at least 51% veteran ownership and veteran control of management and daily operations. The accompanying non-collusion certification, required with competitive bids or contracts exceeding $25,000, records agency and supplier details and certifies no collusion, improper payments, or prohibited employment of former state personnel involved in developing a services contract. It also certifies no boycotts of Israeli goods/services or energy companies, disclosure of specified responsibility matters, and, for physical services, compliance with employee work-eligibility verification requirements.
